subject: Benchmark acceptance handoff + action grid for GreenThread onboarding
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: GreenThread Ops <ops@greenthread.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark acceptance handoff + action grid for GreenThread onboarding

Hi Sara / GreenThread team —

Following our onboarding sync, here’s the acceptance handoff and a concise action grid so we can schedule the formal load run. Goal is to capture the telemetry and artifacts your SRE team needs to sign the perf gate. High-level items below; see attached acceptance template (redwood-acceptance-template.xlsx) and my inline asks.

Acceptance targets (initial):
- Latency: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 200ms for 512-token generation (single-turn API).
- Tail latency: p99 < 450ms during steady state.
- Throughput: sustained 1,200 req/s across the shard set (burst to 2,000 rps tolerated for <5m).
- Error rate: <0.5% 5xx across the run.

Planned load test window and plan:
- Warmup: 10m (cache and KV warms), ramp 0 -> 600 rps.
- Ramp: 30m to 1,200 rps (linear).
- Soak: 60m steady at 1,200 rps.
- Spike: configurable 5m bursts to 2,000 rps to verify graceful degradation/fallback.

Data / access we need from GT:
1) Sample request distribution for sequence lengths (percentiles): 32/128/512 tokens.
2) Keys for readonly telemetry ingest (Prometheus pushgateway endpoint or short-lived API key).
3) Any request/response transforms or post-processing hooks (we need this to ensure measured latency is server-side only).

Action grid (owner / due):
- Deliver sample traffic mix & test user creds: GreenThread Ops (Sara) / EOD Thu 2028-09-07.
- Confirm telemetry endpoint and retention: GreenThread Ops / EOD Thu 2028-09-07.
- Validate test data privacy (PII scrub): GreenThread SRE / Thu 2028-09-07.
- Runbook & rollback criteria: Monica Patel / Fri 2028-09-08.
- Schedule formal run (2-hour window): joint schedule after artifacts received.

Questions:
- Do you want tokenization accounted for client-side or server-side in our measurements? (we typically report server-side model time + transport).
- Any regulatory windows we should avoid for traffic (e.g., production cutovers)?

Next step: Can you confirm the sample traffic and give us a 2-hour slot next week for the run? I’ll loop in Sean for telemetry ingestion.

Thanks —
Elliot
Elliot Price
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
elliot.price@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: redwood-acceptance-template.xlsx (spreadsheet: acceptance criteria, telemetry fields, artifact checklist)

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Sep 2028 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark acceptance handoff + action grid for GreenThread onboarding

Elliot —

Thanks for the clear summary. We can meet those timelines and will supply the traffic mix. Quick clarifications:

1) Tokenization: we prefer you report server-side timings but we will also share a pre-tokenized sample to validate parity.
2) Telemetry: we can provide a read-only Prometheus endpoint with a 24h token (endpoint and credentials will be emailed to you once SAS config is done).
3) Test data: our loader sanitizes PII; we will attach the load scripts and a small sample payload so you can run a smoke test.

Proposed slot for formal run: Tue 2028-09-12 02:00–04:00 UTC (that maps to US morning for your team). If that works we’ll reserve our staging cluster.

Attachments: gt-load-scripts.tar.gz (contains k6 scripts, generator lib, and sample payloads)

Sara Kim
Site Reliability Lead, GreenThread AI
sara.kim@greenthread.ai

Subject: Re: Benchmark acceptance handoff + action grid for GreenThread onboarding

Sara / team —

Appreciate the quick reply and scripts. A few technical notes from the infra side to ensure the acceptance evidence is unambiguous:

- Measurement boundaries: Redwood will send a small latency beacon at the start of each test vector and again on response. Our telemetry will report both transport+model and pure model time (we’ll label metrics model_time_ms and total_time_ms). Please include the generator’s timestamp in payload so we can align.

- Concurrency plan: the 1,200 req/s target assumes average batch size of 1. If you’ll be operating with client-side batching, please confirm effective concurrency and we’ll convert to internal RPCs accordingly.

- Failure and fallback validation: during the spike we’ll intentionally route 10% of requests to a lower-cost model variant to test graceful fallback. If agreeing, we need to document fallback labels so your logs can distinguish degraded results.

- Rollback and stop criteria (short):
  * Abort run if 5xx > 2% sustained for 5min.
  * Rollback to canary config if p99 > 2x target for 15m.

I’ve added a short checklist to the Drive folder (link in the related_links). I’ll prepare the runbook and post it by Fri 2028-09-08. Sean will handle the Prometheus scrape and alert wiring.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

All —

Slot confirmed: Tue 2028-09-12 02:00–04:00 UTC. We’ve uploaded the sanitized traffic mix and instance sizing notes to the Drive folder (same link).

Notes / small updates:
- Our generator will send 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% mid (65-256), 10% long (257-1024).
- We will not use client-side batching for this run (single requests as sent).
- Prometheus endpoint: https://prometheus-gt-staging.greenthread.ai/metrics (read-only token to follow in a separate secure email).

We ran a quick smoke with your k6 scripts against our staging canary and saw a p95 ~230ms at 400 rps — we’ll be interested in the delta once you run from your side.

Attachments: run-window-confirmation.txt (manifest), gt-load-scripts.tar.gz

See you in the run —
